summary.text: One of the fifty daughters of Danaus by the Naiad nymph Polyxo — by lot the bride of Imbrus son of Egyptus when the twelve sons of Aegyptus by Caliadne married the Danaids at Argos; distinct from Evippe daughter of Danaus by the Phoenician woman, bride of Argius.

story.text: Apollodorus lists Evippe ninth among the daughters of Danaus borne on Polyxo — a second Danaid of that name, paired with Imbrus among the Caliadne sons. When the lots were cast Imbrus drew her. On the wedding night she received her father's dagger and, like her sisters, slew her bridegroom — Hyginus counts her among the brides who obeyed Danaus, though his wedding catalogue names only the other Evippe, who killed Agenor.
